title: Dense-source valuative criterion
statement: Let $f:W\to S$ and $h:D\to W$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $h$ quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and with dense topological image. Assume that for every valuation ring $A$ with fraction field $K$, every pair $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to D$ and $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ with $fhu=a|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ has exactly one morphism $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$ satisfying $b|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=hu$ and $fb=a$. Here a valuation ring is a domain $A$ such that every nonzero element of $K$ or its inverse belongs to $A$, and spectra and their induced morphisms are as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $f$ is quasi-compact, it is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $f$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], it is separated. In particular, if $f$ is of finite type and quasi-separated, it is proper. A dense quasi-compact open immersion $D\hookrightarrow W$ is a special case of $h$.

proof.text: We first prove the existence of a lift for an arbitrary square $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$, $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$, with $A$ a valuation ring and $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$, without any compactness assumption on $f$. Choose an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $a(\mathfrak m_A)$. The open $a^{-1}(S_0)$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by the valuation-open lemma. Replace $S,W,D$ by $S_0,f^{-1}(S_0),h^{-1}f^{-1}(S_0)$. Restricting the quasi-compact map $h$ to this open preserves quasi-compactness and density: inverse images of affine opens are the same inverse images as before, and every nonempty open of the restricted target meets $h(D)$. The original unique-lift hypothesis restricts, since a lift over $S_0$ has image in $f^{-1}(S_0)$. Thus we may work over $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

Let $x$ be the image of $\eta$ and choose an affine open $V\subset W$ containing $x$. The scheme $h^{-1}V$ is quasi-compact, so choose a finite affine open cover $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ of it. Since $h(D)\cap V$ is dense in $V$, the union of the finitely many closed sets $\overline{h(T_i)}$ is $V$. Consequently $x\in\overline{h(T_i)}$ for at least one index. Fix this affine scheme $T=T_i$. This is the only place where quasi-compactness of the original source map is used to choose a finite affine cover; no quasi-separatedness of $h$ is assumed.

Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}E$, and let $J=\ker(B\to E)$. The scheme-image interface and affine-kernel node give $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)\hookrightarrow V$ with support $\overline{h(T)}$ and a factor $t:T\to Z$. Here $T\to V$ is quasi-compact since both schemes are affine. The interface gives injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z\to t_*\mathcal O_T$, so its kernel is zero and the scheme-theoretic image of $t$ is all of $Z$. Since $x\in |Z|$, the field point $\eta$ factors uniquely through $Z$. The map $t$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: between affine spectra the inverse image of a principal open $D(b)$ is the affine principal open $D(t^\#b)$, and the diagonal is induced by the surjective multiplication map $E\otimes_{B/J}E\to E$. This justifies using the existing flat-density lemma even in its older quasi-separated formulation.

Put $B_0=B/J$. Form $P=B_0[X_k:k\in K]$ and the $B_0$-algebra map $\pi:P\to K$ sending $X_k$ to $k$ and acting on coefficients through the point $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$. This map is surjective, since every $k$ is the image of $X_k$. The projection $q:\operatorname{Spec}P\to Z$ is flat by the polynomial-projection leaf, and the composition $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}P\to Z\to W$ is $\eta$.

Apply flat density to the quasi-compact, quasi-separated $t:T\to Z$ with scheme-theoretic image $Z$ and the flat $q:\operatorname{Spec}P\to Z$. Thus $H=T\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ has scheme-theoretic image $\operatorname{Spec}P$. This is a map between affine schemes (its source is the spectrum of $E\otimes_{B_0}P$), hence quasi-compact. The scheme-image interface identifies the closure of its topological range with the underlying closed subset of that image, namely all of $\operatorname{Spec}P$. Let $z=\ker\pi\in\operatorname{Spec}P$. The closure-specialization lemma gives a point $v\in H$ whose image specializes to $z$. Apply the specialization-valuation lemma to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}P$, $v$, and $z$. We obtain a valuation ring $A\prime$ with fraction field $K\prime$, a generic map $\operatorname{Spec}K\prime\to H$, and $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}P$, whose closed point maps to $z$, with the square commuting. The generic map therefore factors through $T\to D$.

Let $k\prime=A\prime/\mathfrak m\prime$. The centre equality says that the composite $P\to A\prime\to k\prime$ has kernel $\ker\pi$. Since $\pi$ is surjective, it induces an embedding $\tau:K\hookrightarrow k\prime$. Extend the valuation ring $A\subset K$ along $\tau$ to a valuation subring $A\prime\prime\subset k\prime$ dominating $A$. The valuation-intersection lemma gives $K\cap A\prime\prime=A$ (identifying $K$ with its image under $\tau$).

Form $C=\{c\in A\prime:c\bmod\mathfrak m\prime\in A\prime\prime\}$. The composite-valuation lemma makes $C$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K\prime$ and quotient $C/\mathfrak m\prime\cong A\prime\prime$. The map $R\to A\prime$ from $\alpha$ lands in $C$: its residue is the composite $R\to A\to K\xrightarrow{\tau}k\prime$, which lands in $A\prime\prime$. The generic map $\operatorname{Spec}K\prime\to T\to D$ and this $R\to C$ form a square for the original lifting hypothesis, because the two maps $R\to K\prime$ agree through $P$. Let $g_C:\operatorname{Spec}C\to W$ be its lift.

The two maps $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to W$ given by $\alpha$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}P\to Z\to W$, and by $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}C\xrightarrow{g_C}W$, have the same generic map through $T\to D$. They also have the same composite to $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, since the map $R\to C$ is the restriction of the given $R\to A\prime$. The uniqueness hypothesis for the valuation ring $A\prime$ therefore identifies them.

Restrict $g_C$ along $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime\prime\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C$ using $C/\mathfrak m\prime\cong A\prime\prime$, and call the resulting map $g\prime\prime$. Its generic restriction $\operatorname{Spec}k\prime\to W$ equals $\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)$ followed by $\eta$: the two maps agree by restricting the preceding equality on $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ to its closed-point residue field $k\prime$, and the residue equality $P\to k\prime=\tau\pi$ gives the claimed formula. Its composite to $S$ is the original map $R\to A\subset A\prime\prime$.

Let $w=g\prime\prime(\mathfrak m_{A\prime\prime})$ and choose an affine open $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F\subset W$ containing $w$. The valuation-open lemma implies that all of $g\prime\prime$ factors through $Q$, and the equality of generic restrictions implies that $\eta$ factors through $Q$. Write $\beta:F\to A\prime\prime$ and $\gamma:F\to K$ for these maps. Inside $k\prime$ we have $\beta=\tau\gamma$, so $\gamma(F)\subset K\cap A\prime\prime=A$. Thus $\gamma$ defines $F\to A$ and hence $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Q\to W$ extending $\eta$. Moreover $fb=a$: the two maps $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ agree after composition with $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and on rings $A\hookrightarrow K$ is injective. We have proved existence for every square for $f$, without assuming $f$ quasi-compact.

Existence for all valuation squares persists under every base change $f\prime:W\times_SS\prime\to S\prime$: compose a square with $S\prime\to S$, take the lift to $W$ just constructed, and pair it with the prescribed map to $S\prime$. The fibre-product universal property gives a lift to $W\times_SS\prime$, with the required generic restriction.

Fix such a base change, a point $w\prime\in W\times_SS\prime$, and a specialization $f\prime(w\prime)\rightsquigarrow s$. Apply the specialization-valuation lemma to the morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w\prime)\to S\prime$, its unique point, and $s$. This gives a valuation ring $V$ with fraction field $L$, a map $\operatorname{Spec}V\to S\prime$ centred at $s$, and a generic map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w\prime)\to W\times_SS\prime$. Step 11 gives a lift $b_V$. The generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}V$ specializes to its closed point, so continuity gives $w\prime\rightsquigarrow b_V(\mathfrak m_V)$, and the latter point maps to $s$. Thus every base change of $f$ lifts specializations.

If $f$ is quasi-compact, the universal-specialization criterion applied to step 12 shows that $f$ is universally closed. This proves the first clause. Notice that step 10 needed no quasi-compactness of $f$; that hypothesis is used precisely here.

Now assume only that $f$ is quasi-separated, so its diagonal $\Delta:W\to W\times_SW$ is quasi-compact. A valuation square for $\Delta$ with generic map through $h$ consists of $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to D$ and a pair $a_1,a_2:\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$ over $S$ whose generic restrictions both equal $hu$. The original uniqueness hypothesis gives $a_1=a_2$. This common map is a lift for the diagonal square, and any diagonal lift equals it by the first projection. Therefore $\Delta$ and the same quasi-compact dense $h$ satisfy the unique-lift hypothesis. Apply the universal-closedness argument of steps 1–13 to $\Delta$ to conclude that $\Delta$ is universally closed. This invocation uses the already established argument for an arbitrary morphism; it does not assume quasi-compactness of $f$.

The diagonal is an immersion by the diagonal-immersion lemma. Since it is universally closed, its image is closed, so the immersion-with-closed-image lemma makes it a closed immersion. By definition $f$ is separated. This proves the second clause.

Finally suppose $f$ is of finite type and quasi-separated. Finite type includes quasi-compactness, so steps 13 and 15 give universal closedness and separatedness. Along with finite type these are exactly the definition of properness. For the older unit formulation, separatedness already guarantees uniqueness of valuation lifts, so its existence hypothesis on a dense open $D\subseteq W$ whose inclusion is a quasi-compact morphism supplies the unique-lift hypothesis used here, with $h$ the inclusion.
